column8: For a weapon that grants 1 stack of a debuff on every hit (not a one-shot lump application): total stacks applied/encounter = hits/turn(0.625) x 5 rounds = 3.125. DISCRETE-PAYOUT debuffs (Bleeding, Necrotic -- resolve via one event when a stack decays, no interaction between simultaneous stacks) use total-applied x the keyword's own per-stack rate directly, since individual small stacks mostly resolve before the next one lands, well clear of any stacking taper: e.g. Bleeding = 3.125 x 4 = 12.5. CONTINUOUSLY-ACTIVE debuffs (Slowed, Crippled, Vulnerable, Taunted/Frightened -- penalty applies for as long as any stacks remain, not a discrete event) use a queueing approximation instead: average active stacks = arrival rate/(decay rate - arrival rate) = 0.625/(1-0.625) ~= 1.67, then value = avg active stacks x per-stack rate x 5 rounds: e.g. Slowed = 1.67x1.1x5 ~= 9.2, Vulnerable = 1.67x1x5 ~= 8.35. Flagged as an approximation (simple M/M/1-style queueing model, not an exact combinatorial calculation) -- directionally solid, not exact to the decimal. Assumes this weapon is the sole source of its own debuff (no stacking with a duplicate copy or another item/technique granting the same keyword) -- that's a different character's pricing problem, not this one's.
